# E0352: exported function C can't call

C calls an exported function, so it takes and returns only numbers and `bool`, and its name is a C symbol of its own. Keep the rest of the code inside Stilt.

- Rule: [`c.exported-signatures`](../../reference/20-builds.md#c.exported-signatures)
- Reported at: the part of the signature that C can't take, or the name.
- Tier: `core`, checked in the `types` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0352:2
/// The checksum of a line of text.
pub extern fn checksum(line: str) -> u32 {
  line.len().to_u32() else 0
}
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
/// The checksum of a line of text of `len` bytes.
pub extern fn checksum(len: u64) -> u32 {
  len.to_u32() else 0
}
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0352_exported_function_c_cant_call.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0352_exported_function_c_cant_call.lt):

```text
── EXPORTED FUNCTION C CAN'T CALL ── E0352_exported_function_c_cant_call.lt:2:30  [E0352]

C can't pass a value of type `str`: an exported function takes integers, floats
and `bool`:

  2 │ pub extern fn checksum(line: str) -> u32 {
    │                              ^^^

C calls an exported function, so it takes and returns only numbers and `bool`,
and its name is a C symbol of its own. Keep the rest of the code inside Stilt.
```
